image_description: Two male mallard ducks (drakes) standing on a paved surface with a red brick wall in the background. The duck on the left is viewed from the rear/side, showing its grey body, white tail feathers, and orange webbed feet. The duck on the right is facing forward/right, displaying the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, brown chest, and grey body.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill of the drake on the right is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellowish-green, matching the description.
The eye of the drake on the right is visible and appears dark/black.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both ducks exhibit the typical stocky, compact body shape of mallards with dense-looking plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects display the classic male mallard breeding plumage: iridescent green heads, white neck rings, brown chests, and grey bodies.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs are orange and positioned towards the rear. The feet on the left duck are clearly visible, showing three forward toes connected by webbing.
The wings are folded against the body but appear broad and consistent with duck anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the left shows the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (drake feathers).
